name: Classical Syriac

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Classical Syriac (clas1252).

notes:
Classical Syriac, a Semitic (Afroasiatic, Central Semitic/Aramaic) language written in the Syriac abjad. The 22 consonant letters are mapped to their plosive (non-spirantized) IPA values. Two vowel-letter readings are encoded, both from Noldeke's Compendious Syriac Grammar §4A ('Vowel Expression by Vowel Letters'), which states the distribution directly: waw 'in the middle and end of a word denotes any long or short u or o', and alaph 'denotes every final a and e'. Accordingly non-word-initial ⟨ܘ⟩ reads /u/ (alternatives /o/, consonantal /w/) while word-initial ⟨ܘ⟩ stays /w/, and word-final ⟨ܐ⟩ reads /ɑ/ (alternatives /e/, /ʔ/) instead of the bare glottal stop the base table assigns it. Both readings are confirmed distributionally in the syc_syrc_broad gold: across the 96 headwords there are 27 non-initial ⟨ܘ⟩ occurrences against only 4 gold /w/ tokens and 23 gold /u,o/ tokens, and of the 52 headwords ending in ⟨ܐ⟩ only 19 write a final /ʔ/ at all. Together the two readings move the row from PER 0.4353 to 0.3707.

NOT encoded, and why. ⟨ܝ⟩ (yodh) is NOT given a mater reading. Noldeke §4A licenses one (yodh 'denotes every i in the middle and end of a word, also certain cases of e in the middle'), and encoding it as word-initial /j/ plus /i/ elsewhere was measured at PER 0.3619, 0.9 points below the shipped 0.3707, but the gold distribution refuses it: 39 non-initial ⟨ܝ⟩ occurrences stand against 19 gold /j/ tokens and 24 gold /i,e/ tokens, a near coin flip. The split is morphological, not positional — consonantal yodh is the root consonant of III-y stems and the nisba ending -āyā (ܐܚܝܢܐ /ʔəħjɑnɑ/) — and the engine cannot see morphology, so a positional guess here would be gold-fitting rather than a rule. Left unencoded deliberately.

MEASURED UNDECIDABLE-INPUT CEILING. Not one of the 133 gold rows carries a single combining mark: the Unicode Syriac vowel-point ranges (Eastern seven-dot and Western Serto pointing alike) are entirely absent from the input, while the gold transcriptions are fully vocalised — 235 of the 604 phoneme tokens in the first transcription of each headword (38.9%) are vowels. A spec that emitted perfect consonants and no vowels at all would therefore score PER 0.3863 on this gold, which is the hard floor for a consonant-only Syriac spec and the reason the pre-existing 0.4353 row looked bad. The two vowel-letter readings above are what allows 0.3707 to sit below that floor. Folding every IPA vowel symbol out of both hypothesis and gold and rescoring gives PER 0.2002, so roughly 17 PER points of the remaining error is unwritten vowel quality that no rule can recover from unpointed text.

BEGADKEPAT. The gold does write spirantization — 8 /θ/, 5 /ð/, 4 /f/ and 2 /v/ tokens — but the quššaya/rukkakha dots that mark it (Noldeke §15, §23) never appear in the input, so the alternation is unpredictable here and is left unencoded rather than guessed. Folding the fricative/stop distinction out of both sides (θ→t, ð→d, f→p, v→b) rescores 0.3707 as 0.3454, so unmarked spirantization costs about 2.5 PER points.

PRONUNCIATION TRADITION. Noldeke's Introduction describes the Jacobite (West) and Nestorian (East) traditions as an abiding severance of tradition from the closure of the Academy of Edessa (489) onward, and §4A notes the ā of final alaph 'was pronounced o by the later West-Syrians'. This gold follows neither tradition cleanly: it writes /ɑ/ 112 times and /ɔ/ never, i.e. the classical ā quality rather than the West-Syriac ō, while its begadkepat and its /p ~ f/ tokens are mixed. The spec targets the classical (pre-schism) values that both traditions share and does not claim an Eastern or Western reading.

GOLD COMPOSITION AUDIT (syc_syrc_broad, WikiPron, crowd-scraped from Wiktionary). 133 rows reduce to 96 unique headwords; 30 headwords carry 2-4 conflicting transcriptions (37 extra rows), scored multi-reference. There are no single-letter entries, no alphabet-chart padding and no gloss headwords — the row is free-standing vocabulary. Three transcriptions use non-IPA romanisation characters (ā twice, ī three times) and one contains a stray '(' , which the harness scores as literal segments; that is scrape damage, not a spec error, and the gold is left untouched. Gemination and stress are unencoded.
